Massive water project nears finish line

by Bill Smith September 28, 2026September 28, 2026

Work that started seven years ago to replace a century-old, mile-long water plant intake pipe in Lake Michigan that supplies Evanston’s water plant is nearing completion.

City Council Monday will be asked to approve a ninth, and presumably final, change order with Stantec Consulting Services, the engineering firm on the $51 million project.

The latest change order extends the completion date for Stantec’s work to April 30, 2027. but doesn’t increase the cost.

The pipe being replaced — one of three water intakes at the plant — dates to 1909 and varies in size from 36 to 42 inches. City officials say it had exceeded its useful life.

The new 60-inch pipe will provide increased reliability for the plant in producing the 120 million gallons of water it supplies to customers in Evanston and several other communities.

The project took until 2022 to design and construction work was initially scheduled to be completed by the end of 2024, but city staff say marine construction delays have pushed the anticipated completion of the work to this fall.

The project is funded through federal and state low interests loans for water supply projects. The 30-year, $20 million federal loan has a 2% interest rate, while the 20-year, $31 million state loan has a 1.24% interest rate.

The plant’s other two water intake lines were built in 1956 and 1975.
